factual_claims.claim: Participants in the treatment group used ChatGPT in creative tasks, while those in the control group completed the tasks by themselves.

The findings show that although the boosting effect of ChatGPT was consistently observed over a five-day creative journey, human creative performance reverted to baseline when ChatGPT was down on the 7th and the 30th day.
The use of ChatGPT in creative tasks resulted in increasingly homogenized contents, and this homogenization effect persisted even when ChatGPT was absent.
A global survey by Nature, involving 1600 researchers, reveals that a majority view AI tools as 'very important' or 'essential' for their research in the coming decade.
Sixty-one college students (Mage = 21.56 years, SD = 2.62) with 31 different majors from a university completed the lab experiment.
Participants were tasked with completing two types of creative assignments each day, either independently or with the aid of ChatGPT.
The interrater reliabilities for both novelty and usefulness aspects were satisfactory (ICCs ≥ .90).
Based on the results of Day 1, there was no significant differences on creativity performance between two groups, implying that all participants’ creativity were similar.

unmapped_concepts.reason: The study provides empirical evidence on the long-term effects of AI on human creativity, which is a key situation for understanding AI's impact on human cognitive and creative processes.
unmapped_concepts.Accelerationist Interpretation: The transient nature of the boost is a temporary phase that can be overcome by better integration and training, ultimately leading to higher-order creative capabilities.
unmapped_concepts.Safetyist Interpretation: The regression to baseline and persistent homogenization indicate that AI tools may be fundamentally altering human creative processes in ways that are not yet understood, necessitating caution.
unmapped_concepts.Skeptic Interpretation: The study confirms that AI tools provide only a superficial performance boost that masks a lack of genuine, sustained human creative development.
